newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens bourse ends higher, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse ends higher, seen stabilising.

text.p: The Athens bourse closed slightly higher on Friday with market watchers expecting stabilisation and active block trading to continue by end-96.

"We see a market stabilisation. However, we expect a possible small decline in the share index, in the beginning of January. The public appers to be cautious," said Marietta Petropoulaki of ATE AEDAK.
She added that she expects the stabilisation trend to continue in the first three months of 1997.
"I expect January to be a month of moderate performance and the first signs of improvement to appear around March," said Petropoulaki.
George Chrisochoidis, managing director of N. Chrisochoidis Securities, said he expected the stabilisation trend to continue.
"The financial results of banks and several big Greek companies have been very impressive. Their dividend yields are expected to be high and their stocks quite attractive," Chrisochoidis said.

As soon as the investment public regains confidence in the stock exchange, after audits on the Delta Securities scandal are completed, people will start reinvesting in stocks especially at current prices, he added.

The Athens general share index closed up 0.14 percent or 1.34 points at 934.46 from Tuesday's 933.12. It opened at 932.85. Trading volume fell to 11.5 billion drachmas on volume of 5.3 million shares in active block trading.
Block trades of Intertech, Alpha Leasing, National Investment Bank, Teletypos and National Bank took place.
Losers led gainers 101 to 81 with 36 issues unchanged on 218 traded.
Banks gained 0.89 percent, construction lost 0.25 percent while small caps declined 1.07 percent and investment shares dropped by 0.29 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at the same price at 569.00-587.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, lost 20 drachmas at 4,205.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $8.33-$9.33. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted at 3,341-3,543 drachmas. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
